[EFFECT]
At low to moderate wind speeds (roughly up to about 20 km/h), wind has almost no meaningful effect on predicted bike demand — contributions hover near zero. As wind speed climbs above that threshold, demand is progressively pulled down, with the strongest negative impact at the highest wind speeds (around 50+ km/h), where predicted rentals could be reduced to about 70% of the baseline. The relationship is essentially flat at first, then steadily and noticeably negative.

[IMPORTANCE]
Wind speed is the second least important feature in the model, ranking 8th out of 9 features. Its influence on demand is limited and really only becomes meaningful at quite high wind speeds.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Expecting reduced ridership only during genuinely windy conditions (strong gusts above ~20 km/h) is a reasonable planning approach — there is little need to adjust bike or staff availability on typical low-to-moderate wind days, but scaling back supply during storms or high-wind advisories could help avoid overstocking.
